title: Psalms Chapter 10 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 10 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 10 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 10.

questions.question: In Psalms 10, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The wicked boasteth of his heart's desire
The wicked in his pride doth persecute the poor
The wicked, through the pride of his countenance
He hath said in his heart, I shall not be moved
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked in his pride doth persecute the poor
questions.explanation: This is found in Psalms 10:2, which is the first event described in the chapter.

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask the Lord in Psalms 10:1?
options: Why standest thou afar off, O LORD?
Why dost thou bless the covetous?
Why are thy judgments far above?
questions.correctAnswer: Why standest thou afar off, O LORD?
questions.explanation: This question is directly stated in Psalms 10:1.

questions.question: Who does the wicked persecute according to Psalms 10:2?
questions.correctAnswer: The poor
questions.explanation: This is clearly stated in Psalms 10:2.

questions.question: What does the wicked boast of according to Psalms 10:3?
questions.correctAnswer: His heart's desire
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:3 specifically mentions that the wicked boasteth of his heart's desire.

questions.question: According to Psalms 10:4, what does the wicked not seek after?
questions.correctAnswer: God
questions.explanation: This is stated in Psalms 10:4, where it mentions that the wicked will not seek after God.

questions.question: What are the ways of the wicked described as in Psalms 10:5?
questions.correctAnswer: Grievous
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:5 states that his ways are always grievous.

questions.question: What does the wicked say in his heart according to Psalms 10:6?
questions.correctAnswer: I shall not be moved
questions.explanation: This is explicitly stated in Psalms 10:6.

questions.question: In Psalms 10:2, what does the psalmist wish for the wicked?
options: To be taken in their devices
questions.correctAnswer: To be taken in their devices
questions.explanation: This is mentioned in Psalms 10:2 where it talks about the devices they have imagined.

questions.question: According to Psalms 10:3, whom does the wicked bless?
questions.correctAnswer: The covetous
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:3 states that the wicked blesseth the covetous.

questions.question: What does Psalms 10:5 say about God's judgments?
options: They are far above out of his sight
questions.correctAnswer: They are far above out of his sight
questions.explanation: This is directly stated in Psalms 10:5.

questions.question: According to Psalms 10:1, when does the psalmist feel the Lord is hidden?
questions.correctAnswer: In times of trouble
questions.explanation: The verse Psalms 10:1 states that the Lord hidest himself in times of trouble.

questions.question: True or False: The wicked will seek after God according to Psalms 10:4.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:4 clearly states that the wicked will not seek after God.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist questions why the Lord is far off in Psalms 10:1.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: This is directly stated in Psalms 10:1 where the psalmist asks why the Lord stands afar off.

questions.question: True or False: The wicked believes he will experience adversity according to Psalms 10:6.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:6 states that the wicked believes he shall never be in adversity.

questions.question: True or False: The wicked is described as being humble in Psalms 10:2.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:2 describes the wicked in pride, not humility.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 10 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 10 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 10:7, what is said to fill the mouth of the wicked?
questions.correctAnswer: Cursing and deceit and fraud
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:7 states that 'His mouth is full of cursing and deceit and fraud.'

questions.question: What does Psalms 10:8 promise will happen if someone 'sitteth in the lurking places of the villages' as described in Psalms 10:7?
questions.correctAnswer: He doth murder the innocent
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:8 explains that he ‘sitteth in the lurking places of the villages’ and 'in the secret places doth he murder the innocent,' directly connecting to the behavior described in Psalms 10:7.

questions.question: What imagery does Psalms 10:9 use to describe how the wicked lie in wait for the poor?
options: He lieth in wait secretly as a lion in his den
He stands openly like a shepherd
He waits quietly like a deer
He watches like a bird on a tree
questions.correctAnswer: He lieth in wait secretly as a lion in his den
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:9 uses the imagery of a lion lying in wait secretly in his den to describe the wicked’s ambush on the poor.

questions.question: How do Psalms 10:10 and Psalms 10:11 together describe the attitude and plan of the wicked?
options: The wicked crouches to bring down the poor and believes God has forgotten
The wicked prays for mercy and trusts in God
The wicked is humble and seeks forgiveness
The wicked openly confesses and repents
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked crouches to bring down the poor and believes God has forgotten
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:10 says the wicked 'croucheth, and humbleth himself, that the poor may fall,' and Psalms 10:11 states he 'hath said in his heart, God hath forgotten,' showing the attitude and plan of the wicked are linked.

questions.question: According to Psalms 10:7-8, what is hidden under the wicked's tongue?
questions.correctAnswer: Mischief and vanity
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:7 states that 'under his tongue is mischief and vanity,' describing the hidden evil intentions of the wicked.

questions.question: What secret action does the wicked man do according to Psalms 10:8 that harms the poor?
questions.correctAnswer: He murders the innocent
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:8 says the wicked 'doth murder the innocent' in secret places, highlighting the danger to the vulnerable.

questions.question: Psalms 10:9 describes the wicked’s method of catching the poor. How is this done?
options: By lying in wait secretly and drawing them into a net
By inviting them to a feast
questions.correctAnswer: By lying in wait secretly and drawing them into a net
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:9 clearly states that the wicked 'lieth in wait to catch the poor: he doth catch the poor, when he draweth him into his net.'

questions.question: What is the purpose of the wicked crouching and humbling himself according to Psalms 10:10?
options: So that the poor may fall by his strong ones
questions.correctAnswer: So that the poor may fall by his strong ones
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:10 states the wicked crouches and humbles himself 'that the poor may fall by his strong ones,' indicating a deceptive tactic against the vulnerable.

questions.question: What does the wicked say in his heart about God according to Psalms 10:11?
options: God hath forgotten; he hideth his face
questions.correctAnswer: God hath forgotten; he hideth his face
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:11 states the wicked thinks 'God hath forgotten: he hideth his face; he will never see it,' reflecting his disbelief in divine justice.

questions.question: What plea is made to God in Psalms 10:12?
options: Arise, O LORD; lift up thine hand; forget not the humble
questions.correctAnswer: Arise, O LORD; lift up thine hand; forget not the humble
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:12 is a direct plea for God to act, emphasizing the need for divine intervention for the humble and oppressed.

questions.question: Considering Psalms 10:7-9, what practical lesson can be learned about the behavior of the wicked towards the poor?
options: The wicked use deceit and ambush to harm the poor
The wicked openly help the poor
The wicked ignore the poor completely
The wicked pray for the poor's prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked use deceit and ambush to harm the poor
questions.explanation: These verses describe the wicked as deceitful and lying in wait like a lion to catch the poor, illustrating their harmful tactics.

questions.question: How does the attitude of the wicked in Psalms 10:11 affect their actions described in the previous verses?
options: Their belief that God has forgotten leads them to act with impunity
Their faith in God restrains them
Their fear of God causes them to repent
Their hope in justice makes them fair
questions.correctAnswer: Their belief that God has forgotten leads them to act with impunity
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:11 shows the wicked thinks God has forgotten, which explains why he confidently continues his harmful behavior.

questions.question: What does Psalms 10:12 suggest about the believer’s response to injustice?
options: Believers should pray and ask God to intervene
questions.correctAnswer: Believers should pray and ask God to intervene
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:12 is a plea for God to arise and act, showing that prayer is the appropriate response to injustice.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 10:7 indicates that the wicked’s mouth is full of blessings and truth.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:7 states the wicked’s mouth is full of 'cursing and deceit and fraud,' not blessings and truth.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 10:12 calls on God to forget the humble.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:12 specifically asks God to 'forget not the humble,' so it does not call on God to forget them.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 10 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 10.

questions.question: According to Psalms 10:13, why does the wicked contemn God?
options: He hath said in his heart, Thou wilt not require it.
Because God is too far away.
Because he trusts in his own strength.
questions.correctAnswer: He hath said in his heart, Thou wilt not require it.
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:13 explicitly states that the wicked contemn God because he believes in his heart that God will not require an account from him.

questions.question: In Psalms 10:14, how does God respond to mischief and spite according to the verse?
options: To requite it with thy hand
questions.correctAnswer: To requite it with thy hand
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:14 states God beholds mischief and spite and will requite it with His hand, meaning He will bring justice.

questions.question: What action is requested of God concerning the wicked in Psalms 10:15?
options: Break thou the arm of the wicked and the evil man
questions.correctAnswer: Break thou the arm of the wicked and the evil man
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:15 petitions God to break the strength ('arm') of the wicked and seek out their wickedness until none remains.

questions.question: What declaration about the LORD is made in Psalms 10:16?
options: The LORD is King for ever and ever
The LORD is silent in times of trouble
The LORD is distant from the earth
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD is King for ever and ever
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:16 declares the LORD’s eternal kingship and that the heathen are removed from His land.

questions.question: According to Psalms 10:17, what has the LORD done for the humble?
options: He hath heard their desire and will prepare their heart
He has hidden His ear from them
questions.correctAnswer: He hath heard their desire and will prepare their heart
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:17 states that the LORD hears the desire of the humble and will prepare their heart and listen attentively.

questions.question: What is the purpose, according to Psalms 10:18, for God to judge the fatherless and the oppressed?
options: That the man of the earth may no more oppress
questions.correctAnswer: That the man of the earth may no more oppress
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:18 explains that God's judgment over the fatherless and oppressed aims to end oppression by earthly men.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'mispillah' in Psalms 10:13 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Contemn or despise
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root in Psalms 10:13 translated 'contemn' means to despise or treat with scorn, reflecting the wicked’s attitude toward God.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Psalms 10:14 where God 'beholdest mischief and spite' and the poor 'committeth himself unto thee'?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:14 employs parallelism, a common Hebrew poetic device, contrasting God’s observation of evil with the poor’s trust in Him.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God defending the fatherless and oppressed as seen in Psalms 10:18?
questions.correctAnswer: James 1:27
questions.explanation: James 1:27 emphasizes pure religion as caring for orphans and widows, echoing Psalms 10:18’s theme of God judging for the oppressed and fatherless.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage reflects the plea to 'Arise, O LORD; O God, lift up thine hand' from Psalms 10:12?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 59:16
questions.explanation: Isaiah 59:16 speaks of God seeing and acting against injustice, paralleling the plea in Psalms 10:12 for God to arise and act on behalf of the humble.

questions.question: What comes immediately before the verse that says, 'Wherefore doth the wicked contemn God?' in Psalms 10?
options: Arise, O LORD; O God, lift up thine hand: forget not the humble
The LORD is King for ever and ever
Break thou the arm of the wicked and the evil man
The poor committeth himself unto thee
questions.correctAnswer: Arise, O LORD; O God, lift up thine hand: forget not the humble
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:12 immediately precedes 10:13, calling for God to arise and lift His hand before the question about wicked contemning God.

questions.question: Which literary technique is illustrated by the contrast between the wicked's pride and the humble’s dependence on God in Psalms 10?
questions.correctAnswer: Antithesis
questions.explanation: The chapter contrasts pride of the wicked with the humility of the poor, a clear use of antithesis, highlighting opposing attitudes toward God.

questions.question: How does Psalms 10:11 illustrate the wicked man's perception of God's justice?
options: He believes God hath forgotten and will never see his deeds
questions.correctAnswer: He believes God hath forgotten and will never see his deeds
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:11 reveals the wicked man’s heart, thinking that God has forgotten and hides His face, thus will not see or judge his actions.

questions.question: Which type of parallelism best describes Psalms 10:16's declaration 'The LORD is King for ever and ever: the heathen are perished out of his land'?
questions.correctAnswer: Synthetic parallelism
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:16’s second clause expands on the first by explaining the LORD’s eternal kingship through the outcome for the heathen, a feature of synthetic parallelism.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 10:18 says that God will judge so that oppression by earthly men will continue.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:18 states God judges the fatherless and oppressed so that 'the man of the earth may no more oppress,' meaning oppression will cease.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 10 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 10 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 10:4 teach about human sin?
options: The wicked do not seek after God and exclude Him from their thoughts
All humans are born innocent before God
Sin primarily affects external actions, not internal thoughts
The wicked often seek God in times of trouble
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked do not seek after God and exclude Him from their thoughts
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:4 states, 'The wicked, through the pride of his countenance, will not seek after God: God is not in all his thoughts,' which shows the doctrine that sin alienates humans from God by removing Him from their thoughts.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 10:14 teach about God's providence?
options: God sees all mischief and is a helper to the vulnerable
God is indifferent to human suffering
God punishes only after human judgment
God's providence is limited to the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: God sees all mischief and is a helper to the vulnerable
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:14 says, 'Thou hast seen it; for thou beholdest mischief and spite... thou art the helper of the fatherless,' teaching that God is providentially aware of evil and actively helps the vulnerable.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 10:16 teach about God's kingship?
options: The LORD is King forever and his reign results in the removal of heathen from His land
God's kingship is temporary and limited to Israel
God shares kingship with earthly rulers
God's reign is symbolic but not actual
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD is King forever and his reign results in the removal of heathen from His land
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:16 declares, 'The LORD is King for ever and ever: the heathen are perished out of his land,' affirming God's eternal sovereign reign and His judgment on the nations opposing Him.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 10:14 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Omniscience
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:14 highlights that God 'hast seen it; for thou beholdest mischief and spite,' demonstrating His omniscience in perceiving all wickedness.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 10:17 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:17 says, 'LORD, thou hast heard the desire of the humble: thou wilt prepare their heart, thou wilt cause thine ear to hear,' showing God's faithfulness to His covenant promises to hear and help the humble.

questions.question: How does Psalms 10:1 connect to the theme of God's hiddenness and eventual revelation in Scripture?
options: It expresses the believer's lament over God's apparent absence during suffering, anticipating God's future vindication
It claims God is always visibly present and never hidden
It denies any future revelation of God
It portrays God as indifferent to human affliction
questions.correctAnswer: It expresses the believer's lament over God's apparent absence during suffering, anticipating God's future vindication
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:1 questions, 'Why standest thou afar off, O LORD? why hidest thou thyself in times of trouble?' which reflects the tension of God's hiddenness that is later resolved in biblical revelation and eschatological vindication.

questions.question: How does Psalms 10:18 relate to the biblical theme of justice for the oppressed?
options: It anticipates God's final judgment ensuring oppression ceases
It suggests oppression is permanent and unaddressed by God
It advocates human vengeance over divine justice
It ignores the plight of the oppressed
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates God's final judgment ensuring oppression ceases
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:18 states God's purpose 'To judge the fatherless and the oppressed, that the man of the earth may no more oppress,' which connects to the biblical theme of God's ultimate justice.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 10:6 and 10:11 teach about the wicked's view of God's justice?
options: The wicked presume they will not face adversity and believe God forgets their actions
The wicked fully trust in God's immediate justice
The wicked acknowledge their guilt and seek forgiveness
The wicked are confident in God's mercy towards them
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked presume they will not face adversity and believe God forgets their actions
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:6 says, 'I shall not be moved: for I shall never be in adversity,' and 10:11 states, 'God hath forgotten: he hideth his face,' showing the wicked's arrogant and false presumption about God's justice.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 10:2 and 10:7 teach about the nature of the wicked's actions?
options: The wicked act through pride, cursing, deceit, and fraud against the poor
The wicked's actions are always justified and righteous
The wicked primarily show humility and repentance
The wicked's actions are hidden but harmless
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked act through pride, cursing, deceit, and fraud against the poor
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:2 notes the wicked 'in his pride doth persecute the poor,' and 10:7 says, 'His mouth is full of cursing and deceit and fraud,' describing the sinful character and actions of the wicked.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 10:12 and 10:15 teach about God's response to wickedness?
options: God will arise to act decisively and break the power of the wicked
God passively observes evil without intervention
God punishes only in the afterlife, not in this life
questions.correctAnswer: God will arise to act decisively and break the power of the wicked
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:12 calls God to 'Arise, O LORD; O God, lift up thine hand,' and 10:15 commands, 'Break thou the arm of the wicked,' showing God's active intervention against evil.

questions.question: Skeptics claim that Psalms 10:1-11 teaches God is unaware or uncaring about human suffering. What does Psalms 10:1-11 actually teach?
options: It expresses a lament over God's hiddenness but acknowledges the wicked's arrogant presumption against God's justice
It states God is indifferent and uninvolved in human affairs
It teaches that God approves of the wicked's actions
It claims God is powerless to act
questions.correctAnswer: It expresses a lament over God's hiddenness but acknowledges the wicked's arrogant presumption against God's justice
questions.explanation: Verses 10:1-11 show the psalmist lamenting God's distance ('Why hidest thou thyself in times of trouble?') while describing the wicked's pride and false belief that God forgets them, indicating God's justice is real though not always immediately evident.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 10:5 teach about divine judgment and human pride?
options: The wicked disregard God's judgments because of their pride
God's judgments are always apparent and feared by the wicked
Human pride leads to humility before God
Divine judgment is irrelevant to human behavior
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked disregard God's judgments because of their pride
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:5 says, 'His ways are always grievous; thy judgments are far above out of his sight: as for all his enemies, he puffeth at them,' showing the wicked's pride blinds them to God's judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 10:18 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Justice
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:18 states God's purpose 'To judge the fatherless and the oppressed,' which directly demonstrates the attribute of divine justice.

questions.question: What narrative arc does Psalms 10:9 contribute to within the biblical storyline?
options: It illustrates the ongoing victimization of the poor, setting the stage for God's redemptive intervention
It depicts a world without evil
It emphasizes human ability to overcome sin unaided
It denies the existence of injustice
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates the ongoing victimization of the poor, setting the stage for God's redemptive intervention
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:9 describes the wicked lying in wait like a lion to catch the poor, showing the reality of suffering that prompts God's redemptive justice later in Scripture.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 10:13 teach about the wicked's attitude toward divine accountability?
options: The wicked presume God will not require an account of their actions
The wicked are deeply fearful of God's judgment
The wicked acknowledge God's sovereignty fully
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked presume God will not require an account of their actions
questions.explanation: Psalms 10:13 says, 'he hath said in his heart, Thou wilt not require it,' illustrating the wicked's presumptuous denial of divine accountability.
